A2 Key for Schools Listening Part 1 – identifying key information in five short
dialogues and choose the correct visual.

Description

This lesson plan has been designed to help students prepare for A2 Key for Schools Listening part 1.
This lesson plan can be delivered face to face or online. The ‘online options’ column gives teachers
ideas how the stages could be adapted for teaching online.

Students first do a quiz to see how much they know about A2 Key for Schools Listening Part 1. They
then analyse the questions and work on strategies to help them predict what they will hear. Students
then some independent practice and create their own exam question tasks.

Time required:  60 minutes (can be extended or shortened as required)

Materials        A2 Key for Schools Listening part 1 sample task - identify key
required:            information in five short dialogues and choose the correct visual

                 Prepared presentation/PowerPoint slides

Aims:            to analyse sample questions
                 to introduce skill of prediction to better answer questions
                 to focus students on reading the question carefully

Lead-in Quiz

Tell students you are going to do a quiz.

Read statements about the listening test one at a time and students
indicate yes or no / true or false.

After students respond to each statement, show them the statement and if
it is true or false.

In the listening paper students:

1. hear more information than is shown in the picture. (true)                   as teacher speaking

2. you could hear things about all the pictures in the dialogue. (yes,
    this can be confusing)

3. will hear distractions / things to confuse them e.g. He doesn’t like
    cheese. (yes, so they must listen very carefully)

Remind them that being prepared and knowing what to expect is an
important part of exam preparation.

Today’s lesson will help them practise skills to deal with these aspects of
the task.

Tell students to recap on the process of answering the questions:

    1. Look at the pictures and think of vocabulary relating to them.
    2. Look at the question and underline the key words.
    3. Think about what they are listening for before they hear the audio.
